title: Uncertainty over Uncertainty: Investigating the Assumptions, Annotations, and Text Measurements of Economic Policy Uncertainty

bias_targets.methodology: Re-annotating a sample of news documents and calculating pairwise cross-agreement (PXA) and Krippendorff's alpha to evaluate whether label disagreements stem from annotator bias or inherent semantic ambiguity in the text.

Evaluating algorithmic and prevalence estimation bias by comparing how different text classification models (keyword-matching vs. supervised machine learning) aggregate document predictions, demonstrating that supervised methods can be biased toward the training prevalence.

Analyzing the impact of selection bias in the training dataset (where documents were historically sampled only if they matched specific keyword banks) on downstream model predictions and their correlation with external financial indices like the VIX.
